claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructured state with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The proposed method uses a transformer-based machine-learning model trained on combined multi-fidelity simulation and experimental data.
The model incorporates local chemical-order parameters and spatial strain gradients near incipient cracks through attention-regularization layers.
Local-order and spatial-strain descriptors quantify the multiscale chemical heterogeneity relevant to crack initiation.
Physically regularized attention will emphasize features linking multilevel heterogeneity to elastic, plastic, and fracture behavior.
The proposed attention mechanism will improve feature-extraction efficiency.
The model can improve prediction of Young's modulus for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The model can improve prediction of yield strength for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The model can improve prediction of fracture toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed model will reduce overall computational cost relative to CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, and general machine-learning models lacking explicit multiscale descriptors.
Prediction accuracy will improve by approximately 30–50% over the stated conventional approaches.
Computational cost will be reduced approximately fivefold over the stated conventional approaches.
The model is expected to remain reliable only within the temperature, composition, and microstructural regimes represented in its training data.
Reliability may degrade when cooling rates, phase distributions, experimental conditions, or microstructural phenomena fall outside the training distribution.
The realized accuracy and efficiency gains depend on the quality and representativeness of the multi-fidelity data.
A blinded prospective benchmark will compare predictions with tensile and fracture measurements from newly synthesized HfNbTiVAl10 batches made under conditions similar to the training set.
The benchmark will measure Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness using tensile stress-strain data and J-integral or K_IC fracture tests.

The hypothesis is falsified if the model does not achieve both at least a 30% accuracy improvement and a fivefold computational-cost reduction, or if any property's errors are consistently outside predetermined tolerances.
